title: Temporal persistence: does a written state survive enforced decision boundaries?
question: When a value is written at t and hidden behind a state address, does the system still use that value correctly at t+k after k intervening decision boundaries?
hypothesis: Carry should preserve decision capability across increasing delays; reset and corruption controls should reduce that capability because they remove or alter the persistent representation while leaving hidden world truth and task exposure unchanged.

arms.name: carry
arms.intervention: leave the verified world write intact until the read boundary

arms.name: reset
arms.intervention: clear readable persistent state immediately before the read

arms.name: corrupt
arms.intervention: flip one stored bit immediately before the read

endpoints.name: read_available
endpoints.role: secondary — whether the addressed representation is readable at the decision boundary
endpoints.description: State availability verifies the causal write/read separation before task success is interpreted.

endpoints.name: decision_success
endpoints.role: primary — read-time task success of the state-conditioned decision
endpoints.description: The action is evaluated against hidden environment truth; the router receives only public query/state information.

endpoints.name: router_candidates
endpoints.role: secondary — number of candidates presented to the router

decision_rule.condition: carry decision_success remains above the reset/control condition at a delay k
decision_rule.licenses: the persistent state contributes causally at that delay under the registered task and router.
decision_rule.does_not_license: long-horizon memory in general or semantic memory quality.

decision_rule.condition: carry collapses with increasing k while reset is similar
decision_rule.licenses: the tested state-conditioned mechanism does not preserve useful information across that delay.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that all persistent-state architectures fail at that horizon.

decision_rule.condition: carry and reset are indistinguishable because state availability is not changed as intended
decision_rule.licenses: nothing; the intervention failed and the run is a design failure.

held_constant: candidate count and task generator are fixed at H=64
the hidden environment reference is never passed to the router or index
the same router and executor are used across arms
each probe enforces all intervening decision boundaries
learning writes are disabled during the measurement so only the declared world write changes persistence
results contain no scientific status field
the measured read boundary uses H=64; intervening filler decisions use two candidates solely to enforce causal passage without adding an unmeasured workload term

amendments.old_definition: Each intervening decision boundary was generated with the full H=64 candidate population.
amendments.new_definition: Each intervening filler decision boundary uses one candidate; the measured read boundary remains H=64.
amendments.rationale: The full-H filler generation dominated runtime without affecting the declared read-time decision endpoint. The causal boundary is preserved while removing unneeded computational work from non-measured filler decisions.
amendments.discovered: The first registered run exposed excessive runtime before producing a result.
amendments.affected: Execution cost of filler-only boundaries; no change to read-boundary H, delay levels, arms, seeds, primary endpoint, or hidden-truth boundary.
amendments.no_result_under_previous_version: The first run had no emitted result/artifact before this amendment.

amendments.old_definition: Intervening filler decisions use one candidate.
amendments.new_definition: Intervening filler decisions use two candidates, the minimum accepted by the benchmark generator.
amendments.rationale: The benchmark generator requires n_candidates >= 2. This correction changes only the filler workload and keeps the read-boundary task at H=64.
amendments.discovered: The first A1 amended smoke/measurement invocation failed before producing an artifact because the generator rejects one-candidate tasks.
amendments.affected: Filler-only workload; no change to read-boundary H, delay levels, arms, seeds, primary endpoint, or hidden-truth boundary.
amendments.no_result_under_previous_version: No scientific result was produced under A1 before this correction.
